raw_chat.content: You have reached the step limit. Do not call any more tools. Reply now with your final answer: a short summary of what you found and what you changed.

The issue was caused by a regression in `FieldRenderer.list_to_class` within `src/bootstrap4/renderers.py`. The code assumed that every `<label>` element found within the enclosing `div` would have a direct child input element accessible via the `label.input` attribute (which appears to be a custom property or intended usage of BeautifulSoup objects in this context, although standard BeautifulSoup uses `label.find('input')`). When a `<label>` did not contain an `<input>`, `label.input` returned `None`, leading to an `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'attrs'`.

I fixed this by adding a check to ensure `label.input` is not `None` before attempting to access its attributes.

```python
<<<<
            for label in enclosing_div.find_all("label"):
                label.attrs["class"] = label.attrs.get("class", []) + ["form-check-label"]
                label.input.attrs["class"] = label.input.attrs.get("class", []) + ["form-check-input"]
====
            for label in enclosing_div.find_all("label"):
                label.attrs["class"] = label.attrs.get("class", []) + ["form-check-label"]
                if label.input:
                    label.input.attrs["class"] = label.input.attrs.get("class", []) + ["form-check-input"]
>>>>
```

Note: I am assuming `label.input` is a valid way to access the input in this codebase's specific environment/extension of BeautifulSoup, as evidenced by the traceback. If it were standard BeautifulSoup, it would likely be `label.find('input')`. I have maintained the existing style.
